command: (review only -- the claim is the artifact)

assumptions: evidence_rank is a MAX over per-act ranks, not a sum and not a path composition. Both alternatives were rejected at design time because each makes the attestation cycle profitable: summing lets ten signatures outweigh one measurement

FIRST STATED WRONGLY. The original theorem was the stronger claim that attestation cycles are INERT, evidence_rank(G) = evidence_rank(G - C). The test falsified it in under a minute with assert 0 == 1: when the ring is the only support, removing it drops ATTESTED to NONE. An attestation is not nothing, it is bounded. The theorem was corrected, not the test

this is the finite shadow of the Payor/Loeb situation -- box(box P -> P) -> box P fails when the boxes belong to different parties who only quote each other. NO claim is made about the modal statement; only the finite one is implemented and tested
observed_result.question_for_the_reviewer: I first claimed the STRONGER result that attestation cycles are inert and my own test falsified it within a minute. Is the corrected version also wrong? Is a MAX over per-act ranks the right aggregation, or does it discard information a lattice would keep? Does the Payor/Loeb analogy overreach -- I claim only the finite shadow.
observed_result.statement: For a witness graph G and an attestation cycle C on the same claim, evidence_rank(G + C) = max(evidence_rank(G), ATTESTED). No number of mutually-attesting parties reaches REVIEWED or INDEPENDENT: a ring in which A vouches for B, B for C and C for A passes every producer != verifier check while nobody has computed anything.

typed_remainders.comparison: a review binds a reading of an argument to a commit; it does not bind a number to a measurement, and it cannot promote this claim
